buy.subscription: {#strong}Subscription.{/strong} Monthly or yearly, renewing until you cancel. It starts at once on your consent. [pending legal review] The refund rule for a subscription is waiting for review.
buy.key: {#strong}Time key.{/strong} Prepaid, bought once, for 7, 30, 90 or 365 days. A key gives exactly what a subscriber of the same plan has for the same number of days.
buy.key-time: A key adds time to your account, up to 36 months.
buy.key-refund: An unredeemed key is refundable in full within 14 days of purchase, and expires 12 months after purchase. [pending legal review]
buy.key-limits: 2 keys per order, and 4 per account per sale window or per rolling 30 days.
buy.key-bind: A key is non-transferable and binds to your account when you activate it. [pending legal review]
buy.credits: {#strong}Usage credits.{/strong} Prepaid units of Kolwen’s own metered service. They are used only at Kolwen and cannot be moved to anyone else or cashed out. Unused credits are refundable at the price you paid, within 14 days. [pending legal review] Whether credits expire has not been decided yet.

subprocessors.title: Subprocessors
subprocessors.intro: These are the providers that process personal data of Kolwen's customers on Kolwen's behalf: what each one does, where it processes the data, the basis for any transfer abroad, and the data processing agreement it is under. Paddle is listed for transparency: it acts as its own controller for purchase data. Each row takes effect on the day that row's provider first holds a customer's data. Until then the row says so.

row1.purpose: Serving the site and the service: hosting, Workers and their storage, and logs.
row1.data: Requests made to the site, as Cloudflare handles them to serve it.
row1.where: Cloudflare's network, and sub-processors outside the European Economic Area, Switzerland and the United Kingdom, in countries the agreement does not name.
row1.basis: EU Standard Contractual Clauses (Module Two and Module Three); the UK Addendum; the Swiss addendum; the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework where Cloudflare is certified under it.
row1.retention: Kept until the main agreement ends or the processing is no longer needed. After that, Cloudflare deletes or returns the data at the customer's choice, except where the law requires it to keep it. The agreement states no fixed number of days.
row1.from: from the day it first holds customer data.

row2.purpose: Account sign-in, and the service's database.
row2.data: Account identity (name and e-mail address) and password hashes.
row2.where: The project's region, chosen when the account is created, from the regions Supabase lists. The project's database and sign-in are hosted in that region. Supabase's agreement says covered data may be processed anywhere Supabase or its sub-processors maintain facilities, and its regional commitment gives way where the law or the requested service requires it. Account and support data are covered data under that rule. Service telemetry goes to systems segregated from customer projects; the agreement names no region for it.
row2.basis: EU Standard Contractual Clauses (Module Two and Module Three), with the UK and Swiss addenda, where data leaves the EEA, the United Kingdom or Switzerland.
row2.retention: A copy may be requested within 30 days after the agreement expires; after that the data is deleted, including copies held by sub-processors. The agreement states no number of days for completing the deletion.
row2.dpa: Data Processing Agreement, Version 1, 1 August 2026; accepted before the account holds customer data.
row2.from: from the day it first holds customer data.

row3.purpose: Merchant of record for purchases: payment and tax. Paddle acts as its own controller for purchase data.
row3.data: The buyer's name, e-mail address, and payment and tax data.
row3.where: Paddle's controller entities in the United Kingdom, the United States, Ireland and Canada; its processors anywhere in the world.
row3.basis: EU Standard Contractual Clauses (Module One, controller to controller), and the UK Approved Addendum, for transfers from the United Kingdom or the EEA to countries without an adequacy decision.
row3.retention: No fixed period. Kept while the customer relationship continues or as the law requires, and for the limitation period and a short administrative period after it. Kept also while a claim, investigation or dispute is open.
row3.dpa: None as a processor: Paddle acts as its own controller under its Data Sharing Addendum.
row3.from: from the day it first holds customer data.

row4.data: E-mail address, message content and message metadata.
row4.where: The United States, where Resend's primary processing takes place, and its sub-processors there.
row4.basis: EU Standard Contractual Clauses (Module Two and Module Three); the UK SCCs; the EU SCCs as adapted for Switzerland; the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, under which Resend states it complies.
row4.retention: Deleted within 90 days of account termination. The agreement states no period for message content or logs.
row4.from: from the day it first holds customer data.

row5.provider: An off-provider backup store (named before the first customer data is stored there).
row5.purpose: Encrypted backup copies of account and billing records.
row5.data: As held in those records, encrypted.
row5.from: from the day it first holds customer data.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.intro: This page is Kolwen's accessibility statement for the website at kolwen.com. It is dated 1 November 2026.

h.checked: What is checked on every change

accessibility.what: Kolwen's website describes a chatbot product that is still in development. No product ships yet, and the home page says so. The site is a set of static pages in English and Thai, which a visitor reads in a browser.
accessibility.commitment: Kolwen aims to make the website usable by people with disabilities, and to fix a problem that a visitor reports.
accessibility.target: Kolwen's own target is WCAG 2.2 level AA. It is a target Kolwen set for itself. It is not a legal test, and this statement does not claim that the site meets it.
accessibility.checked: The repository runs these checks in its continuous integration on each pull request and each push to main, and a failed check fails the change. A headless browser checks every page, in English and Thai: text reflows at 320 CSS pixels wide without sideways scrolling; text at 200 percent is not cut off; the browser reports no content-security-policy violation; the language switch sets the page's language. On the reading pages, text and background meet a contrast of 4.5 to 1 (3 to 1 for large text) in both the light and the dark colour scheme, the line height is at least 1.5 times the font size, and the line length of English text is measured against 80 characters. The source checks confirm that the home page declares English as its language, and that the layout uses relative type sizes and a viewport setting that does not block zoom.
accessibility.limits: The checks above cover only what they measure. They do not test every criterion of WCAG 2.2. In particular, no check reads the keyboard focus order or whether focus is visible; no check reads the names and roles of controls with a screen reader; the contrast and line-height checks cover the reading pages, not the default pages, whose background gradient is not read; the line-length check does not apply to Thai text; and the pages have not been checked with script switched off. The repository records no manual audit and no test with assistive technology by people.
accessibility.prereq: The site needs a current browser. It needs no plug-in, and no account or sign-in to read a page. Whether a page reads with script switched off is not checked.
accessibility.report: If a page is hard for you to use, write to info@kolwen.com with the address of the page and what got in your way. We read every report and answer it. We do not promise a time for the answer.
